text.approach: Begin at the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead off US-2 (~2,950 ft). Climb via Mahar Creek Ridge to Merritt Lake, then continue over Mt. Mastiff's Southeast Ridge and Mt. Howard's Northeast Ridge (both reported as snow climbs/rock scrambles) before dropping to the Howard-Rock col and climbing Rock Mountain's northeast side.

text.overview: A cross-country mountaineering line up Rock Mountain's northeast side, reached by crossing the Howard-Rock col at the far end of a multi-summit Nason Ridge traverse (Mt. Mastiff - Mt. Howard - Rock Mountain), rather than via the maintained West Route trail.
text.descent: From the summit, descend the South Ridge and East Slope toward Rock Lake, picking up the maintained Rock Mountain Trail in the Rock Lake basin and following it down the switchbacks to the Rock Mountain Trailhead on US-2 (a different trailhead than the Old Merritt Lake start, so a car shuttle or hitch on US-2 is typically needed).

identifiedBy.fact: Begin at the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead off US-2 (~2,950 ft)

lastAnswer.notes: Trailhead named by route text; the only placement is the USFS 'Merritt Lake Trailhead' (the route says 'Old'; the old road start may sit a little lower than this point, ~2,950 ft stated). WTA pages do not give Merritt Lake coordinates; wenatcheeoutdoors 403. Descent ends at the Rock Mountain TH (USFS 47.775232,-120.957772; WTA 47.7757,-120.9581, agreeing within ~60 m), a different trailhead, so a shuttle is needed.

text.approach: From Newhalem, drive or walk SR 20 east about 12 miles (0.4 mi west of Horsetail Creek, ~2.8 mi northeast of Colonial Creek Campground) to a turnout at about 1,900 ft elevation, directly across from a large boulder field on Ruby's northwest side.

text.overview: A steep, direct hike/scramble straight up Ruby's northwest ridge from a Highway 20 turnout — the most popular way up during winter and spring, when SR 20 is gated for the season.
text.descent: Retrace the ascent ridge, using snow ramps to negotiate cliff bands in winter/spring conditions; remove snowshoes for one cliffy section around 4,000 ft as needed on the way down as well.

text.approach: Via the multi-day Goodell Creek approach to a camp on the Chopping Block ridge (~6,400 ft) or the col separating the peak from the main Picket Range; from there, walk and scramble (some exposed 3rd class) southwest to the base of the ridge.

text.overview: The peak's classic technical route: 4 pitches of alpine rock up the northeast ridge, established by the Firey party in 1970, with a steep 5.5 crux about 100 ft below the summit.
text.descent: Descend by rappelling the ridge itself — most parties use a 70m rope to reach most stations comfortably; one reporting party got down on a 50m rope with a tagline. Existing fixed rap slings have been reported along the route.

identifiedBy.fact: Pickets approaches (incl. Chopping Block, Approaches 6/7) start at the end of Goodell Creek road near Newhalem; route text also says Goodell Creek approach

lastAnswer.notes: Route's own text names Goodell Creek; a page confirms the Goodell Creek road-end start for Chopping Block. No page gave a coordinate and no official point matches; report signed name only (OSM match by script). Mountaineers page 403.

text.overview: A new route rather than the peak's first ascent, climbed in 1961 by Ed Cooper and Glen Denny, ascending to the base of the north ridge, diagonally traversing the northwest face, and topping out via the west ridge. A 2008 party described a similar line as starting up the NE Ridge before an exposed class-4 traverse across the north face gains the NW ridge for an easy class-3 finish.
text.descent: Rather than reverse the exposed class 4 ledges of the north face, rappel the Northeast Ridge on a single rope, using the fixed slings along it, back to the camp on the Chopping Block ridge (about 6,400 ft). The way out from there is long and steep: work across Stump Hollow, a mix of snow, slab and heather, up to the Barrier crest, follow a faint path down the crest from timberline (about 5,600 ft)

identifiedBy.fact: Chopping Block reached by Goodell Creek road-end approaches; route text names Goodell Creek approach

lastAnswer.notes: Same as NE Ridge: same camp and approach. No coordinate found.

text.overview: The technical line up Pyramid's east side, climbed as the 5th of 14 summits during the first complete Southern Pickets Enchainment; rated II 5.8, with rock the first party found 'surprisingly beautiful' despite the peak's chossy reputation.

lastAnswer.notes: Page (stephabegg.com Pickets) has Pyramid reached via Goodell Creek and Crescent Creek Basin, but nothing about this East Ridge specifically; peak-level inference only, same as prior pass. Goodell Creek is the only Southern Pickets approach found, so likely but not established for this route.

Lead still Snow Lakes Trailhead (WTA 47.5441,-120.7097 opened; USFS 47.544106,-120.709515), via Nada Lake 5.2 mi, per search results for the Mountaineers West Side page; both Mountaineers pages return 403 so no opened page ties this route. WTA Snow Lakes page does not mention Temple. Weak.

text.approach: Same general Southern Pickets approach as the South Route — via Goodell Creek, The Barrier, and Crescent Creek Basin — continuing to the notch/saddle between Himmelhorn and West Twin Needle rather than climbing directly from the basin.

text.overview: The peak's original 1932 line: a moderate class 2 scramble up the west slope from the Himmelhorn-West Twin Needle notch, most often climbed today as one link in the multi-day Southern Picket enchainment/traverse; continuing off the summit onto the class 3 east arete toward East Twin Needle is part of the full traverse rather than a stand-alone descent.
